public_rationale: The records confirm the reserved-symbol example and repeated mistakes. They also describe an apparently unrecovered name-conflict episode. However, the available edited records do not securely establish how often syntax failures occurred or whether the unrecovered episode was actually caused by syntax. This supports parts of the claim without settling its full frequency-and-recovery assertion.
limitations: The arbitrary-problem document is a 2024 revision describing the 2023 tests.
General interface failures cannot all be counted as syntax failures.
A locally corrected error can coexist with an incorrect final answer.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In the tests, GPT-4 often made syntax errors calling Wolfram Alpha and sometimes could not correct them.

statement.excerpt: GPT-4 often made syntactic mistakes in calling Wolfram Alpha (e.g. it tried to use a reserved word as a variable) and was sometimes unable to correct itself and find a correct formulation.
statement.document_title: Getting GPT to work with external tools is harder than you think

from_speaker: a reserved word as a variable
our_interpretation: Syntactic mistakes includes invalid symbol use, as Marcus's own example specifies; it is not restricted to parser errors.
Often means a recurring feature of the experiment, not merely several retries within one exceptional problem.
Failure to recover must concern the tool-call formulation, rather than an independently incorrect mathematical model.
The claim concerns the June–August 2023 experiment.
criteria.support_condition: The records establish recurring invalid Wolfram formulations across problems and cases where subsequent attempts never produced a valid formulation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently complete review establishes that such errors were isolated rather than recurring, or that all were successfully corrected.
